claimsToVerify: Vomitoriums in ancient Rome were architectural exit passageways, not rooms for vomiting.
The exact meaning of the gladiator thumb gesture (pollice verso) is historically uncertain and debated among scholars.
Togas were heavy, uncomfortable, and generally avoided by everyday Romans in favor of simple tunics.
Ancient Roman marble statues were originally painted in bright, vivid colors rather than left plain white.
